newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: NBS-Boland shares up, lift financial index.
newsitem.headline: NBS-Boland shares up, lift financial index.

text.p: Shares in recently-merged banking group, NBS-Boland Ltd rose on Thursday amid speculation on moves by the firm to reshuffle some of its interests, dealers said.

By 1130 GMT shares in NBS-Boland, which is now South Africa's fifth largest banking group, had added 200 cents to 102.00 rand, a new 1997 high for the stock. Some 38,700 shares valued at 3.95 million rand had changed hands.
Dealers said NBS's climb had pushed the financial index to a fresh year high of 9,763.2 -- a gain of 23.3 points.
"The main one that's driving the financial index up is NBS. I think this could still be part of the deal involving NBS, Boland and BOE," one dealer said.
"They are under a cautionary at this stage and that's why things are happening," he added.
NBS said on May 23 that BOE Natwest Ltd, a stockbroking unit in the group, was in talks with Real Afrika Durolink. It gave no further details.
Sine the merger of NBS and Boland, Boland shares as well as shares in its pyramid holding company, Samgro Investment Holdings Ltd, have been suspended.
There has been much speculation recently on how the group will structure its various interests.

Shares in the Board of Executors Ltd (BOE), which earlier this year bought a 22.2 percent stake in NBS while at the same time the NBS Boland group bought a 24.3 percent stake in BOE, also peaked in earlier trade.
Shares touched a new year high of 156 rand but had since come off to trade at 154.50 rand -- a gain of 50 cents.
